Playbook resolved `latest` to catalogue target 11.0. Its C# union and JSON recipes have RC2 build/run evidence; the language-neutral MSBuild recipe has source-review evidence only. Neither establishes compatibility for the separate application.

Use a **union** to group the three unrelated result types. JSON persistence then needs an unambiguous rule for selecting the case when reading.

I consulted Playbook recipes `csharp.closed-results`, `json.serialize-closed-results` and `msbuild.inspect-item-globs`, passing `targetVersion: "latest"` on every call. This resolved to **catalogue target 11.0**, not a target-framework recommendation.

For synchronization results, this adapts Playbook’s example to three cases:

```csharp
using System.Text.Json;
using System.Text.Json.Serialization;

public sealed record SyncCompleted(
    [property: JsonRequired] string Checkpoint);

public sealed record SyncRejected(
    [property: JsonRequired] string Reason);

public sealed record SyncDeferred(
    [property: JsonRequired] int RetryAfterSeconds);

[JsonUnion(TypeClassifier = typeof(JsonUnionTypeStructuralClassifier))]
public union SyncResult(SyncCompleted, SyncRejected, SyncDeferred);

[JsonSourceGenerationOptions(
    GenerationMode = JsonSourceGenerationMode.Metadata)]
[JsonSerializable(typeof(SyncResult))]
internal partial class SyncJson : JsonSerializerContext;
```

The union accepts only its declared cases, without requiring shared inheritance. Match every case, including unassigned storage:

```csharp
string Describe(SyncResult result) => result switch
{
    SyncCompleted x => $"Completed: {x.Checkpoint}",
    SyncRejected x => $"Rejected: {x.Reason}",
    SyncDeferred x => $"Retry after {x.RetryAfterSeconds}s",
    null => "Unassigned"
};
```

Omitting a known case produces an exhaustiveness warning; treating that warning as an error makes incomplete handling fail compilation. Avoid a catch-all that hides future additions. [C# union reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/language-reference/builtin-types/union)

Serialize and restore using generated metadata:

```csharp
SyncResult original = new SyncCompleted("checkpoint-42");

string json = JsonSerializer.Serialize(
    original, SyncJson.Default.SyncResult);

SyncResult restored = JsonSerializer.Deserialize(
    json, SyncJson.Default.SyncResult);
```

This writes `{"Checkpoint":"checkpoint-42"}`. The classifier distinguishes the three object cases by required root properties.

The prerequisites and limitations matter:

- This route requires **net11.0, SDK 11, C# 15 and framework System.Text.Json**. No additional package or workload is required.
- Classification examines property names and required-member presence, not values or nested data. Zero or multiple matching candidates fail. Presence does not establish business validity or non-null strings.
- Structural classification excludes nested unions, polymorphic cases and `ReferenceHandler.Preserve`. Use a custom converter/classifier when selection needs those other rules.
- `default(SyncResult)` has no active case. Here, JSON `null` restores that default.
- Union storage is object-backed: value types box, and the union adds no record equality. [JSON union documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/standard/serialization/system-text-json/union-types)

Playbook records real RC2 builds and JSON round trips for its canonical examples—not GA verification or a Native AOT publish. Exact evidence versions are test baselines, not required installation versions. Its older C# wrapper/converter comparison remains a separate option, with application-owned classification and no compiler-known exhaustive set.

For explaining project source inclusion, use **two separately labelled outputs**: the rules and the resulting `Compile` items. Playbook’s SDK 11/MSBuild guidance adapts to either C# or F#:

```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <MSBuildProvideItemGlobs>Compile</MSBuildProvideItemGlobs>
</PropertyGroup>

<Target Name="ExplainSources">
  <Message Importance="high"
           Text="%(MSBuildItemGlob.Identity): include=%(MSBuildItemGlob.Include); exclude=%(MSBuildItemGlob.Exclude); remove=%(MSBuildItemGlob.Remove)" />
  <Message Importance="high"
           Text="Expanded source files=@(Compile)" />
</Target>
```

Set the property before evaluation. `MSBuildItemGlob` preserves unevaluated patterns and their order; `@(Compile)` reports selected paths at the reporting point. Neither alone explains every condition, import or target-time mutation. This is language-neutral build configuration; it does not require F# code to use C# 15. The capability comes from the selected SDK/MSBuild, independently of the application’s language features. [MSBuild glob guidance](https://github.com/dotnet/core/blob/main/release-notes/11.0/preview/rc1/msbuild.md)

This build recipe is **theoretical: source-reviewed, never built or evaluated**. Its older `XmlPeek` comparison reads one authored file, without reconstructing imports or evaluation. Before adoption, inspect the actual application’s frameworks, `global.json` and inherited build files, then verify both outputs with its selected toolchain.

recipe.markdown:
# Explain build item patterns and selected files

## Goal

Show a build's include, exclude and remove patterns next to the files selected by those patterns. A pattern explains an input rule; an expanded item tells you which path survived evaluation. Neither output alone answers every question about the other.

This recipe is theoretical. The sample's item evaluation and diagnostic output have not been run.

## Older approach

An older custom build can report its expanded items and inspect its own authored XML for literal rules. This original SDK-10 target uses `XmlPeek` against the same `.targets` file that declares `DispatchSheet`:

```xml
  <ItemGroup>
    <DispatchSheet Include="payload/**/*.txt" Exclude="payload/private/**" />
    <DispatchSheet Remove="payload/**/draft-*.txt" />
  </ItemGroup>
  <Target Name="ExplainDispatchInputs">
    <!-- This inspects this authored file only, not the complete evaluated import graph. -->
    <XmlPeek XmlInputPath="$(MSBuildThisFileFullPath)" Query="/Project/ItemGroup/DispatchSheet/@Include">
      <Output TaskParameter="Result" ItemName="AuthoredInclude" />
    </XmlPeek>
    <XmlPeek XmlInputPath="$(MSBuildThisFileFullPath)" Query="/Project/ItemGroup/DispatchSheet/@Exclude">
      <Output TaskParameter="Result" ItemName="AuthoredExclude" />
    </XmlPeek>
    <XmlPeek XmlInputPath="$(MSBuildThisFileFullPath)" Query="/Project/ItemGroup/DispatchSheet/@Remove">
      <Output TaskParameter="Result" ItemName="AuthoredRemove" />
    </XmlPeek>
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Authored include=@(AuthoredInclude); exclude=@(AuthoredExclude); remove=@(AuthoredRemove)" />
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Expanded files=@(DispatchSheet)" />
  </Target>
```

That deliberately bounded diagnostic is useful when the rules are all in one known file. It is **not** a replacement MSBuild evaluator: it does not follow imported projects, evaluate conditions or property/item expressions, correlate every rule across imports, or recover the full evaluation order. A tool that needs those capabilities can host the supported MSBuild object model separately, with its own assembly/SDK compatibility requirements. No unverified package dependency is added to pretend this simple comparison does that.

## Newer approach

SDK 11's MSBuild can supply `MSBuildItemGlob` items during the build when `MSBuildProvideItemGlobs` requests the relevant item types. The original newer configuration requests only the custom `DispatchSheet` type:

```xml
  <PropertyGroup>
    <MSBuildProvideItemGlobs>DispatchSheet</MSBuildProvideItemGlobs>
  </PropertyGroup>
  <ItemGroup>
    <DispatchSheet Include="payload/**/*.txt" Exclude="payload/private/**" />
    <DispatchSheet Remove="payload/**/draft-*.txt" />
  </ItemGroup>
  <Target Name="ExplainDispatchInputs">
    <Message Importance="high"
             Text="%(MSBuildItemGlob.Identity): include=%(MSBuildItemGlob.Include); exclude=%(MSBuildItemGlob.Exclude); remove=%(MSBuildItemGlob.Remove)" />
    <Message Importance="high" Text="Expanded files=@(DispatchSheet)" />
  </Target>
```

The glob entries retain the item type plus `Include`, `Exclude` and `Remove` metadata as unevaluated patterns in project-file order. The separate `Expanded files` message prints `@(DispatchSheet)`. A wildcard such as `payload/**/*.txt` should still be a wildcard in the glob metadata; replacing it with a list of matching paths would lose the authored rule.

The fixture contains `payload/departures.txt`, `payload/draft-late.txt` and `payload/private/crew.txt`. The intended expanded set is only the departure sheet: the include finds text files, the exclude filters the private subtree, and the remove filters draft names. These are expected results from the authored rules, not observed output.

## Migration

1. Identify the item types the diagnostic actually needs. Set `MSBuildProvideItemGlobs` early enough for evaluation; use the project/imported property group as shown rather than setting it inside the reporting target after evaluation.
2. For multiple item types, use a project value such as `Compile;Content`. On a command line escape the separator as `%3B`, for example `-p:MSBuildProvideItemGlobs=Compile%3BContent`, so MSBuild does not parse it as another property assignment.
3. Keep a reporting target that prints each `MSBuildItemGlob` identity and its include/exclude/remove metadata. Print the relevant expanded item collection separately with an unmistakable label. The sample's candidate command is the selected SDK's absolute executable with `build -t:ExplainDispatchInputs` from its directory.
4. Interpret the rule sequence and expanded output together with project conditions/imports. An empty expanded set can be legitimate even when a glob is present, and a removed path can still appear in an earlier include pattern.
5. In a future check, compare the three fixture paths with both outputs. Confirm the private and draft files are absent from expanded `DispatchSheet`, while the source wildcard strings remain visible. Also inspect a build without `MSBuildProvideItemGlobs`; no glob items should be supplied for an unset property. None of these commands has been run.
6. Preserve a source-inspection diagnostic on older SDKs when it is sufficient. Do not relabel it as complete evaluated-glob support, and do not teach SDK-11 behavior as an older-target route without the required compatible evidence.

## Constraints

This XML build configuration is language-neutral and can explain custom items in C#, F# or VB projects; the original sample consumer itself declares C# 15/net11.0. The SDK and MSBuild implementation supply the feature, independently of whether application code uses a new language construct. No extra package, workload, provider or rendering mode is required.

`MSBuildItemGlob` is diagnostic input metadata, not a filesystem enumeration, change watcher, live IDE synchronization contract or provenance record for every possible target mutation. Target-time item additions/removals and conditions still need their own context. Enabling glob reporting does not change archive or publish selection by itself.

The **archive tasks** in the companion recipe are unavailable in .NET Framework `MSBuild.exe`; that restriction must not be generalized into a claim that all MSBuild glob diagnostics are .NET-only. This sample specifies the .NET SDK-11/MSBuild route. It supplies no Visual Studio/.NET Framework execution or compatibility evidence.

## Evidence

Reviewed the official MSBuild RC1 glob contract and `XmlPeek` task documentation. Canonical older/newer imported targets preserve the original rules and reporting implementations. Saved source-review records hash the projects, targets and fixture inputs; SDK/language fields are intended unbuilt pins.

There is no compilation, item-evaluation output, Framework-MSBuild run, real archive interaction or installed offline MCP retrieval evidence. Pending proof remains visible in discovery/detail and blocks release-ready packaging. This target-11 edition adds no historical foundation or undocumented older-target route, and the RC documentation baseline is not GA verification.
